pathSubtitle: Practice the language of job interviews — from first impressions to tough questions and salary negotiation.

lessons.title: First Impressions
lessons.completionSummary: You have completed First Impressions successfully

questions.prompt: Why is Sam at the office?
options: To deliver a package
For a job interview at ten
To meet a friend
questions.feedback: Correct! Sam is at the office for a job interview at ten.

questions.prompt: What does the HR assistant offer Sam?
options: Coffee
Water
A biscuit
questions.feedback: Correct! The HR assistant offers Sam water.

questions.prompt: What does "interview" mean?
options: to greet someone who has arrived
to sit down
a meeting where someone asks you questions for a job
questions.feedback: Correct! "interview" means a meeting where someone asks you questions for a job.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the correct use of "welcome"?
options: I have a job interview on Monday.
Please take a seat and wait.
Welcome to our office!
questions.feedback: Correct! "Welcome to our office!" is a good example.

questions.prompt: What does "take a seat" mean?
options: a meeting where someone asks you questions for a job
to greet someone who has arrived
to sit down
questions.feedback: Correct! "take a seat" means to sit down.

lessons.title: Tell Me About Yourself
lessons.completionSummary: You have completed Tell Me About Yourself successfully

questions.prompt: What did the candidate study?
options: Marketing
Business Management
Computer Science
questions.feedback: Correct! The candidate studied Business Management.

questions.prompt: Why does the candidate's manager give them urgent tasks?
options: They are slow
They are reliable and finish on time
They have nothing else to do
questions.feedback: Correct! The manager gives them urgent tasks because they are reliable and finish on time.

questions.prompt: What does "apply" mean?
options: a job or role in a company
a duty or task you are in charge of
to make a formal request for a job or course
questions.feedback: Correct! "apply" means to make a formal request for a job or course.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the correct use of "position"?
options: I applied for three jobs last week.
I want more responsibility in my next job.
She is applying for the manager position.
questions.feedback: Correct! "She is applying for the manager position." is a good example.

questions.prompt: What does "responsibility" mean?
options: to make a formal request for a job or course
a job or role in a company
a duty or task you are in charge of
questions.feedback: Correct! "responsibility" means a duty or task you are in charge of.

lessons.title: Handling Tough Questions
lessons.completionSummary: You have completed Handling Tough Questions successfully

questions.prompt: What mistake did the candidate make?
options: Sent an email to a wrong address
Sent a report to the wrong client
Forgot a deadline
questions.feedback: Correct! The candidate sent a report to the wrong client.

questions.prompt: What is the candidate's weakness?
options: Being too slow
Difficulty delegating tasks
Poor communication
questions.feedback: Correct! The candidate's weakness is difficulty delegating tasks.

questions.prompt: What does "mistake" mean?
options: to say sorry for something you did wrong
to recognize and value something
something done incorrectly or wrongly
questions.feedback: Correct! "mistake" means something done incorrectly or wrongly.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the correct use of "apologize"?
options: Everyone makes mistakes — what matters is how you fix them.
She appreciated my honesty.
I apologized to the client immediately.
questions.feedback: Correct! "I apologized to the client immediately." is a good example.

questions.prompt: What does "appreciate" mean?
options: something done incorrectly or wrongly
to say sorry for something you did wrong
to recognize and value something
questions.feedback: Correct! "appreciate" means to recognize and value something.

lessons.title: Salary Negotiation
lessons.completionSummary: You have completed Salary Negotiation successfully

questions.prompt: What salary range does the candidate request?
questions.feedback: Correct! The candidate requests $55,000–$60,000.

questions.prompt: What does the candidate ask about when the salary is low?
options: Company size
The full package and benefits
Working hours
questions.feedback: Correct! The candidate asks about the full package and benefits.

questions.prompt: What does "salary expectations" mean?
options: planned a specific amount of money for something
the total set of pay and benefits offered
the amount of pay you hope to receive
questions.feedback: Correct! "salary expectations" means the amount of pay you hope to receive.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the correct use of "budgeted"?
options: What are your salary expectations for this role?
The full package includes salary, bonus, and health insurance.
We budgeted $50,000 for this position.
questions.feedback: Correct! "We budgeted $50,000 for this position." is a good example.

questions.prompt: What does "package" mean?
options: the amount of pay you hope to receive
planned a specific amount of money for something
the total set of pay and benefits offered
questions.feedback: Correct! "package" means the total set of pay and benefits offered.

lessons.title: Senior-Level Strategic Interview
lessons.completionSummary: You have completed Senior-Level Strategic Interview successfully

questions.prompt: What did the candidate do first to tackle the customer service problem?
options: Fired the team
Conducted a root-cause analysis
Hired more staff
questions.feedback: Correct! The candidate first conducted a root-cause analysis.

questions.prompt: How did customer satisfaction scores change?
options: From 58% to 81%
From 40% to 80%
From 70% to 90%
questions.feedback: Correct! Customer satisfaction scores rose from 58% to 81%.

questions.prompt: What does "transformation" mean?
options: a method of identifying the original cause of a problem
a point of congestion that slows down a process
a fundamental and thorough change in form or character
questions.feedback: Correct! "transformation" means a fundamental and thorough change in form or character.

questions.prompt: Which sentence shows the correct use of "root-cause analysis"?
options: The new CEO led a complete transformation of the company.
The approval process was a major bottleneck.
We carried out a root-cause analysis before proposing any solutions.
questions.feedback: Correct! "We carried out a root-cause analysis before proposing any solutions." is a good example.

questions.prompt: What does "bottleneck" mean?
options: a fundamental and thorough change in form or character
a method of identifying the original cause of a problem
a point of congestion that slows down a process
questions.feedback: Correct! "bottleneck" means a point of congestion that slows down a process.
